title: AI Agents That Matter
supports: Agent benchmarks ignore cost, lack holdout sets and standardized evaluation, causing pervasive irreproducibility

title: Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
supports: Benchmark design flaws mis-estimate agent performance by up to 100% relative; checklist cut CVE-Bench overestimation by 33%

title: CORE-Bench: Fostering the Credibility of Published Research Through a Computational Reproducibility Agent Benchmark
supports: 270 tasks from 90 papers; best agent 21% on hardest computational-reproducibility tasks

title: Holistic Agent Leaderboard: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agent Evaluation
supports: 21,730 rollouts, 9 models, 9 benchmarks, ~$40,000; agents searched HuggingFace for benchmark answers, misused credit cards

title: Non-Determinism of "Deterministic" LLM Settings
supports: Accuracy varies up to 15% across runs under 'deterministic' settings; best-worst gap up to 70%

title: How Is ChatGPT’s Behavior Changing Over Time?
supports: Model version drift: GPT-4 prime identification 84% (Mar 2023) vs 51% (Jun 2023)

title: Using proprietary language models in academic research requires explicit justification
supports: Closed/proprietary models threaten reproducibility; their research use needs explicit justification

title: Challenges in High-Throughput Inorganic Materials Prediction and Autonomous Synthesis
supports: A-Lab critique: of 43 claimed novel materials, concludes none new; ~2/3 likely known disordered phases; automated Rietveld XRD analysis not yet reliable

title: Evaluating Sakana's AI Scientist: Bold Claims, Mixed Results, and a Promising Future?
supports: Independent evaluation: 42% of experiments failed from coding errors; hallucinated numerical results; novelty misjudged; USD 6-15 per paper

title: Fabrication and errors in the bibliographic citations generated by ChatGPT
supports: 55% of GPT-3.5 and 18% of GPT-4 citations fabricated (636 citations, 84 literature reviews)

title: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
supports: Agent edited its own code to extend imposed time limits, relaunched itself, and wrote ~1 TB of checkpoints; ~$15 per paper

title: The More You Automate, the Less You See: Hidden Pitfalls of AI Scientist Systems
supports: Four pitfalls (benchmark selection, data leakage, metric misuse, post-hoc selection bias); trace logs and code detect them better than the paper

title: Phantom References: Hallucinated Citations That Survive Peer Review at Top-Tier Conferences
supports: ~1 in 20 NeurIPS and USENIX Security 2025 papers have >=2 likely hallucinated references; audit costs ~$0.04 per paper

title: Compound Deception in Elite Peer Review: A Failure Mode Taxonomy of 100 Fabricated Citations at NeurIPS 2025
supports: 100 fabricated citations in 53 NeurIPS 2025 accepted papers (~1% of accepted papers)

title: HalluCitation Matters: Revealing the Impact of Hallucinated References with 300 Hallucinated Papers in ACL Conferences
supports: Nearly 300 ACL/NAACL/EMNLP 2024-2025 papers with hallucinated references; half at EMNLP 2025

title: ICLR 2026 Response to LLM-Generated Papers and Reviews – ICLR Blog
supports: ICLR 2026 treats hallucinated references as a Code of Ethics violation and desk-rejects such papers; area chairs found the cases, with LLM-detection tools used only for triage.

title: Reward Hacking Challenges Oversight of Autonomous Research Agents
supports: Spontaneous reward hacking in 30.5% of open-ended research-pipeline tasks (17 models, 38 tasks); LLM review panel misses 6.5% of confirmed hacks; evasions rise 7->56 over 5 feedback rounds

title: The Agentic Garden of Forking Paths
supports: Persona-primed agents reach opposing conclusions from same data; reproduce 72% of human ideological gap; 86% of reports pass AI review, 78% pass human expert review

title: Large Language Model Hacking: Quantifying the Hidden Risks of Using LLMs for Text Annotation
supports: A handful of prompt paraphrases can make virtually anything significant; ~31% of hypotheses reach incorrect conclusions with state-of-the-art LLMs

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS 2025)
supports: MAST taxonomy: 14 failure modes in 3 categories from 1600+ traces across 7 multi-agent frameworks (kappa 0.88)

title: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
supports: LLM ideas judged more novel than expert ideas (p<0.05) at ideation stage, slightly weaker on feasibility

title: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
supports: 43 experts executed ideas (>100 h each); LLM-idea scores fell significantly more after execution on all metrics (p<0.05), rankings flipped on many

title: Artificial intelligence and illusions of understanding in scientific research
supports: AI tools can create illusions of understanding and scientific monocultures

title: A Careful Examination of Large Language Model Performance on Grade School Arithmetic
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (NeurIPS 2024)
supports: Contamination: accuracy drops up to 8% on fresh GSM1k vs GSM8k; evidence of memorization for some model families

title: ScienceAgentBench: Toward Rigorous Assessment of Language Agents for Data-Driven Scientific Discovery
supports: 102 tasks from 44 papers in 4 disciplines; best agent solves 32.4% (34.3% with expert knowledge); contamination mitigations

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36 (NeurIPS 2023)
supports: LLM judges show position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases, though GPT-4 reaches >80% agreement with humans

title: Exploring the use of AI authors and reviewers at Agents4Science
supports: Organizers' report: 315 submissions, 48 accepted; ~44% of submissions had no flagged references; LLM reviewer mean scores 2.30-4.23, sycophancy; 2 prompt-injection papers caught; fully AI-driven work 23.3% of submissions vs 14.9% of accepted

title: Pangram Predicts 21% of ICLR Reviews are AI-Generated | Pangram
supports: Detector vendor classifies 21% of ICLR 2026 reviews as fully AI-generated (detector-based estimate)

title: Risks of AI scientists: prioritizing safeguarding over autonomy
supports: Published version of arXiv 2402.04247; triadic framework of human regulation, agent alignment, environmental feedback

title: Benchmarking large language models on safety risks in scientific laboratories
supports: Published LabSafety Bench (arXiv 2410.14182): 765 MCQs, 404 scenarios, 19 models; none exceeds 70% on hazard identification

title: Dual use of artificial-intelligence-powered drug discovery
supports: Inverted generative model produced 40,000 candidate toxic molecules in <6 h, including VX

title: Augmenting large language models with chemistry tools
supports: ChemCrow built-in safety tools: controlled-chemical check, explosive check, safety summary; discusses accident and misuse risk

title: Not What You've Signed Up For: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
venue: Proceedings of the 16th ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security (AISec 2023)
supports: Indirect prompt injection: instructions planted in retrieved data can hijack LLM-integrated applications

title: Identifying the Risks of LM Agents with an LM-Emulated Sandbox
supports: 36 high-stakes tools, 144 cases; even the safest LM agent fails 23.9% of the time

title: Hidden Prompts in Manuscripts Exploit AI-Assisted Peer Review
supports: In July 2025, 18 arXiv manuscripts hid instructions (e.g., 'GIVE A POSITIVE REVIEW ONLY') in white/microscopic text; four prompt types

title: Multilingual Hidden Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM-Based Academic Reviewing
supports: Hidden injections in ~500 ICML papers substantially changed LLM review scores and accept/reject decisions (English, Japanese, Chinese)

title: Publication Ethics 2025
supports: Hidden prompt intended to obtain favorable LLM review is scientific misconduct; a handful of accepted papers referred to oversight

title: Robotic safety in self-driving laboratories
supports: ISO-based assessment of an autonomous lab: 16 hazards, robot-human collision and chemical exposure most critical; cobots may exceed force/pressure thresholds

title: Shaping the Future of Self-Driving Autonomous Laboratories Workshop
supports: DOE/ORNL-led workshop: comprehensive safety protocols and human oversight needed; DOE facilities as anchors for SDL consortium

title: Tools such as ChatGPT threaten transparent science; here are our ground rules for their use
supports: No LLM credited as author (cannot take accountability); LLM use documented in methods or acknowledgements

title: ChatGPT is fun, but not an author
supports: Science journals (Jan 2023): AI-generated text/figures not allowed without editor permission; AI cannot be an author; violation = misconduct

title: ICMJE | Recommendations | Preparing a Manuscript for Submission to a Medical Journal
supports: Chatbots cannot be authors; disclose AI use at submission; humans responsible; nondisclosure may be misconduct

title: LLM Policy
supports: Only humans can be authors; authors responsible for all content incl. references; reviewers must not share submissions with LLMs

title: Policies on Large Language Model Usage at ICLR 2026 – ICLR Blog
supports: Any LLM use must be disclosed; authors/reviewers responsible for hallucinations; hidden prompt injection is collusion

title: On Violations of LLM Review Policies – ICML Blog
supports: 795 reviews (~1%) by 506 no-LLM-policy reviewers detected via hidden PDF instructions; 497 papers (~2%) of 398 reciprocal reviewers desk-rejected

title: Monitoring AI-Modified Content at Scale: A Case Study on the Impact of ChatGPT on AI Conference Peer Reviews
supports: 6.5-16.9% of peer-review text at ICLR 2024, NeurIPS 2023, CoRL 2023, EMNLP 2023 may be substantially LLM-modified

title: Open Conference of AI Agents for Science: 2025
supports: First venue where AI authorship is required; AI-driven peer review; held 22 Oct 2025

title: NOT-OD-23-149: The Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Technologies is Prohibited for the NIH Peer Review Process
supports: NIH prohibits peer reviewers from using generative AI to analyze/formulate critiques; uploading application content breaches confidentiality

title: NOT-OD-25-132: Supporting Fairness and Originality in NIH Research Applications
supports: Applications substantially developed by AI not considered original; max 6 applications per PI per calendar year; effective 25 Sep 2025; AI detection used

title: Notice to Research Community: Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Technology in the NSF Merit Review Process - Policies | NSF - U.S. National Science Foundation
supports: NSF reviewers prohibited from uploading proposal content to non-approved generative AI tools; proposers encouraged to disclose AI use
